name: get_state
title: See the current scene
description: Call FIRST. Returns a summary of the current project, scene, and active shot: the placed entities (id, asset, label, position) and the choreography marks on the timeline (actor + camera). Coordinates are in meters, +X is right, -Z is forward/away from the default camera; heading 0 faces -Z; rotationDeg turns counter-clockwise seen from above (90 faces -X).

name: list_assets
title: List things to place
description: List the placeable asset catalog (people, animals, vehicles, furniture, environment kits, primitives). Use an assetId from here with add_entity. Optionally filter by category. People include the Mixamo mocap bots person.mocapMale / person.mocapFemale (Y Bot / X Bot) when the local Mixamo library is installed.

name: add_entity
title: Place something
description: Place a new entity on the ground. x/z in meters (+X right, -Z away); rotationDeg turns counter-clockwise seen from above: 0 faces -Z, 90 faces -X. A labelled entity gets its own colour automatically so the video model can tell people apart. Returns the new entity id and its colour.

rotationDeg.description: Optional heading in degrees, counter-clockwise seen from above; 0 faces -Z, 90 faces -X.

color.description: Optional colour: red, amber, green, blue, purple, pink, teal, orange, or a hex value like "#e5484d".

name: move_entity
title: Move something
description: Reposition an existing entity. Omitted fields are left unchanged.

y.description: Optional height in meters above ground.

rotationDeg.description: Optional heading in degrees, counter-clockwise seen from above; 0 faces -Z, 90 faces -X.

name: delete_entity
title: Remove a person or object
description: Remove a person, vehicle or object from the scene, with its marks. Weapons it was holding are set down where its hands were. Pass name so the approval card says what goes.

name.description: What it is in a few words, shown on the approval card, e.g. "the spear" or "HERO". Display only.

name: list_weapons
title: List weapons
description: The weapons a person can hold (swords, knives, axes, spears, staffs, bats, a shield, pistol, rifle, shotgun, bow): assetId, kind, one- or two-handed and the usual hand. Also lists who holds what in the current scene.

name: hold_weapon
title: Put a weapon in someone's hand
description: Put a weapon in a person's hand. Give assetId (from list_weapons) to make a new one in their hand, or weaponId to pick up one already in the scene. It follows the hand through every move, gait and fight; two-handed weapons bring the other hand onto the grip. Whatever that hand held is set down. Returns the weapon id, hand and colour.

entityId.description: The person who holds it (entity id from get_state).

assetId.description: A weapon assetId from list_weapons, e.g. "prop.sword" — makes a new one in the hand.

weaponId.description: An existing weapon's entity id — picks it up instead.

hand.description: Left or right hand (default: the weapon's usual hand — R, but L for the bow and the shield).

name: drop_weapon
title: Drop a weapon
description: Let go of a held weapon. It stands on the ground where the hand was at the playhead.

weaponId.description: The held weapon's entity id (get_state shows heldBy).

name: add_actor_mark
title: Add an actor mark
description: Drop a timeline mark for an actor entity: at time t (seconds) the actor is at x,z. Chain marks to choreograph a walk. gait sets the movement style between marks.

time.description: Time of the mark in seconds.

name: add_camera_mark
title: Add a camera mark
description: Drop a camera mark at time t: camera at x,y,z (meters, y is height) looking with panDeg (counter-clockwise seen from above: 0 faces -Z, 90 faces -X) and tiltDeg (positive looks up, negative down). focalLength in mm on Super 35 (24 wide, 35 normal, 50-85 tight).

y.description: Camera height in meters above ground.

panDeg.description: Pan in degrees, counter-clockwise seen from above; 0 faces -Z, 90 faces -X (left).

tiltDeg.description: Tilt in degrees; positive up, negative down.

time.description: Time of the mark in seconds.

name: clear_camera_marks
title: Clear the camera marks
description: Remove all camera marks from the active shot (keeps actor marks).

name: frame_shot
title: Frame the shot
description: Frame the camera with shot words, e.g. "MCU on B, over A's right shoulder, 50mm" or "two-shot of A and B, low angle, from the left at 2.5s" — or the same fields structured. The camera mark is re-solved every frame from the subjects' live positions, so the framing holds while they move. Updates the camera mark at that time (±1 frame) or adds one. Names are entity labels or names from get_state. Over a shoulder: that shoulder stays in frame near the edge and the subject's eyes sit on the far third, as near the upper third as the size allows; size sets the distance (with no lens it sets the lens); angle raises or lowers the camera and backs it off when it must, so with a lens the frame can come out looser; overhead counts as high and side is ignored. When lens, size and angle can't all hold, the returned achievedSize says what the frame is. The camera stays in open space with the subject in view: when the asked-for view is blocked by the set or other cast (or would sit inside a wall or a body), it comes closer on a wider lens (same frame size), rises, or swings round the subject, the nearest clear choice first, and the result's note says what blocked it and what changed; a warning says when no clear view exists. A clear view is framed exactly as asked.

words.description: Shot words: size (EWS WS FS MS MCU CU ECU, wide, close-up…), on <name>, two-shot of <a> and <b>, over <name>'s left|right shoulder, <n>mm, eye level / low angle / high angle / overhead / ground level, from the front|behind|left|right, 3/4 left|right, profile, dutch <deg>, at <t>s.

size.description: Shot size (with subjectIds, instead of words).

subjectIds.description: Entity ids from get_state to frame; two or more make a group shot.

entityId.description: Entity whose shoulder the camera looks over.

over.description: Over-the-shoulder framing: the camera sits behind this entity's shoulder, which stays in frame.

side.description: Where the camera sits relative to the first subject's facing (its own right is right); line = side-on to the two subjects.

angle.description: Camera height (default eye level). Over a shoulder, overhead counts as high and the camera rises or drops only as far as keeps the shoulder in frame (it backs off to get there).

lens.description: Focal length in mm (default: the mark's lens).

time.description: Mark time in seconds (default: the playhead).

name: list_fight_moves
title: List fight moves
description: The moves a fight script can use, with their aliases, default target and impacts (which hand/foot/elbow/knee lands, when, and its peak speed in m/s), then the gun shots, which need a gun in hand: "shoot" / "fire" play the gun's own aim, rifle-aim-fire (shouldered) for the rifle and shotgun and pistol-aim-fire for the pistol (each lists its guns).

name: stage_fight
title: Stage a fight
description: Stage a scripted two-person fight blow by blow: every hit lands on its frame, defenses are up in time, knockback follows the physics, and the report gives each blow's contact error (warnings flag blows the bodies can't reach). Spawns fighters A and B at x/z (facing each other across headingDeg; assets and labels choose their bodies and names) unless fighterIds names two people. weapons puts a weapon in each fighter's usual hand: blows from it land with the blade or point ("A sword slash to head -> parry"), blocks meet the defender's blade or shield, and "A shoot to body -> hit" fires a held gun along a line through the target. Fighters keep weapons they already hold. Set props count: a fight that spawns its fighters moves up to 3 m to keep clear of them, push-backs stop at them, and the report warns when a path still runs into one. A shot too short for a beat grows to the whole fight (up to 60 s; the report says so). Returns the fight id, its script text and the report.

script.description: Fight script, one blow per line (or ';'): <who> <move> [to head|body|legs] [-> outcome, ...] [power 0.2-1] [at <t>s]. who = A / B or a fighter label; outcomes hit, block, parry, slip, duck, miss, ko (one per impact). Example: "A jab cross to head -> block, hit\nB hook to body -> hit power 0.9".

beats.description: Beats as objects instead of a script.

move.description: Strike id or alias from list_fight_moves.

outcomes.description: One per impact; shorter lists are padded with block for earlier impacts.

ending.description: End on a KO (default) or with both standing.

random.description: Write a random script for the shot's length instead.

headingDeg.description: Facing of the staging in degrees, counter-clockwise seen from above (0 faces -Z, 90 faces -X); the fighters stand side by side across it.

fighterIds.description: Two person entity ids from get_state to fight (keeps their look and spots).

assets.description: [A's, B's] body for the fighters it spawns: person asset ids from list_assets, e.g. ["person.mannequinMale", "person.mannequinFemale"] or the mocap bots ["person.mocapMale", "person.mocapFemale"] when listed (default man and woman). Not with fighterIds.

labels.description: [A's, B's] label for the fighters it spawns (default "A", "B"); the script may name them by it. Not with fighterIds.

coverage.description: Camera coverage built from live shot words: master (wide two-shot), punch-in (MCU on big hits), over-shoulder (per beat), follow (handheld on the attacker). Sizes open up for held weapons and falls (see fight_coverage).

weapons.description: [A's, B's] weapon: an assetId from list_weapons (e.g. "prop.sword", "prop.pistol") or null to leave that fighter as they are.

name: update_fight
title: Change a fight
description: Re-solve a staged fight with a new script / beats, exaggeration or camera coverage. Replaces only the two fighters' marks. Returns the fight id, script and report.

fightId.description: Fight id from stage_fight or get_state.

script.description: Fight script, one blow per line (or ';'): <who> <move> [to head|body|legs] [-> outcome, ...] [power 0.2-1] [at <t>s]. who = A / B or a fighter label; outcomes hit, block, parry, slip, duck, miss, ko (one per impact). Example: "A jab cross to head -> block, hit\nB hook to body -> hit power 0.9".

beats.description: Beats as objects instead of a script.

move.description: Strike id or alias from list_fight_moves.

outcomes.description: One per impact; shorter lists are padded with block for earlier impacts.

coverage.description: Camera coverage built from live shot words: master (wide two-shot), punch-in (MCU on big hits), over-shoulder (per beat), follow (handheld on the attacker). Sizes open up for held weapons and falls (see fight_coverage).

name: fight_coverage
title: Cover the fight with the camera
description: Replace the active camera with beat-aware coverage of a staged fight, built from live shot words and kept on one side of the fight line: master (one wide two-shot), punch-in (a two-shot that pushes in on the defender at every big hit), over-shoulder (per beat, high over the attacker's shoulder so the guard stays under the defender's face), follow (per beat, a handheld two-shot led by the attacker). Every framing keeps the blow in frame: sized to the target (head MCU, body MS, legs FS), a knockdown or KO a wide two-shot of both fighters, and weapons wider (an armed punch-in still pushes in, to an MS two-shot); an over-shoulder beat with a weapon, a fall or a blow to the legs becomes a two-shot on the line (FS; WS for a sword, katana, spear or long gun). Clears the camera's aim lock. Each framing keeps a clear view of the fighters past the set and other cast over its beat (closer on a wider lens, higher, or swung up to 60° on its side of the line); views lists the framings that moved, with a note, or a warning when none is clear.

fightId.description: Fight id from stage_fight or get_state.

side.description: Which side of the fight line, as fighter A sees B (default: the side the camera is on now).

name: get_fight
title: Read a fight
description: A staged fight's script text and its solver report (per beat: impact times, contact error, reactions, warnings).

fightId.description: Fight id from stage_fight or get_state.

name: delete_fight
title: Remove a fight
description: Forget a staged fight. The fighters and their marks stay on the timeline; the fight can no longer be re-solved.

fightId.description: Fight id from stage_fight or get_state.

name: set_shot
title: Change shot settings
description: Update the active shot settings. Omitted fields are unchanged. A new fps or duration re-solves the shot's staged fights (impacts on the new frame grid; beats past a shorter end are left out and listed in the returned fights' warnings).

name: new_shot
title: Add a shot
description: Create a new shot in the current scene (same blocking, fresh camera). Returns the new shot.

name.description: Optional name for the new shot.

name: apply_framing
title: Frame the shot
description: Auto-frame the camera using a preset relative to the subjects: 2S (two-shot), OTS (over-the-shoulder), REV (reverse), TOP (top-down), LOW (low angle), DUTCH (canted). Pass entityIds to frame those entities; otherwise the selection, else the people in the scene. The camera stays in open space with every subject in view for the whole shot: a pose behind a wall or blocked by the set or other cast moves to the nearest clear one (closer on a wider lens, higher, or swung round), and the result's note says so; a warning says when no clear view exists.

entityIds.description: Optional entity ids from get_state to frame (2S and OTS need two).

name: list_action_presets
title: List vehicle and object moves
description: List motion-path presets for non-character performers: plane takeoff/landing/flyby, helicopter orbit, bird swoop, car chase moves, falling debris, thrown objects. Call before apply_action_preset.

name: apply_action_preset
title: Give something a move
description: Lay a full motion path (with altitude) on an entity from its current pose: plane-takeoff, heli-orbit, car-chase-weave, debris-fall… Replaces the entity's existing marks.

name: list_sequence_styles
title: List crowd sequence styles
description: List the styles available per sequence type for spawn_sequence (dance styles, fight formats, chase modes).

name: spawn_sequence
title: Stage a crowd sequence
description: Stage a whole choreographed crowd in one call: N dancers performing together, a paired brawl or mob fight, a foot chase, or a car chase. Creates the performers AND their choreography. Position with x/z/headingDeg (heading 0 faces -Z). A fight of count 2 is solved by the Fight Director (blows land; returns fightId); bigger fights are crowd choreography where blows don't connect. For a scripted fight where blows land, use stage_fight.

style.description: Style id from list_sequence_styles (e.g. a dance preset id, "paired", "weaving").

name: list_choreography_options
title: List choreography options
description: Discover the choreography vocabulary before spawn_choreography / choreograph_entities: the kinds (dance/fight/chase), the styles per kind, the dance formations, and the endings per kind.

name: spawn_choreography
title: Stage a dance, fight or chase
description: Stage a full choreography routine — a dance number, a paired or one-vs-many fight, or a foot chase — spawning fresh performers AND their per-beat blocking in one call. Reads as real staged choreography: dances hit on the count and change formation, fights are paired attack→reaction exchanges that stay in range, chases run a serpentine path with near-misses. Position with x/z and headingDeg (heading 0 faces -Z). Call list_choreography_options for the vocabulary. A fight with 2 performers is solved by the Fight Director (blows land on their frame; returns fightId); with more it is crowd choreography where blows don't connect. For a scripted fight where blows land, use stage_fight.

performers.description: Number of performers (dance 1-40, fight 2-8, chase 2-6; clamped per kind).

durationS.description: Seconds to fill (defaults to the active shot duration).

style.description: Style id from list_choreography_options (dance: hiphop/party/latin/robot/mixed; fight: brawl/martial-arts/sparring).

canon.description: Dance: stagger performers into a wave (canon).

mirror.description: Dance: mirror odd performers (fight: mirror stances).

formationChange.description: Dance: walk to a fresh formation between phrases.

ending.description: Fight: finish | sparring. Chase: caught | escape.

seed.description: Optional PRNG seed for repeatable results (randomized if omitted).

name: choreograph_entities
title: Choreograph existing people
description: Retarget existing PERSON entities into a choreography routine: keeps their assets and labels but replaces their timeline with a fresh dance/fight/chase built around the group. Same routine options as spawn_choreography, plus entityIds. The performer count comes from the list and the routine centers on the group, so there is no x/z. A fight between exactly 2 people is solved by the Fight Director (blows land; returns fightId). For a scripted fight where blows land, use stage_fight with fighterIds.

durationS.description: Seconds to fill (defaults to the active shot duration).

canon.description: Dance: stagger performers into a wave (canon).

mirror.description: Dance: mirror odd performers (fight: mirror stances).

formationChange.description: Dance: walk to a fresh formation between phrases.

ending.description: Fight: finish | sparring. Chase: caught | escape.

name: list_motion_presets
title: List performer motions
description: List the single-performer motion-preset library (fight / dance / gesture / everyday / sport / stunt) as { id, name, category, duration }. These are the motions choreography routines are built from. Optionally filter by category.

name: list_camera_moves
title: List camera moves
description: List the classic camera-move presets (orbits, cranes, drone follows, vertigo dolly-zoom, whip pan…) with ids, categories, and descriptions. Call before apply_camera_move.

name: apply_camera_move
title: Move the camera
description: Apply a classic camera-move preset to the active shot camera: generates a full set of camera marks over the shot built around a subject, riding along if the subject moves (e.g. drone-follow a flying plane). Track-style moves also enable aim-lock. Replaces the camera's existing marks. A follow move on a person (follow-behind, lead-the-subject, side tracks …) keeps the camera out of walls and bodies with the person in view past the set and other cast, moving or adding marks where needed; the result's note says how, and a warning says when no clear view exists for part of the shot.

entityId.description: Subject to build the move around. Omit to use the selected entity, else the first person, else the first vehicle or prop (never the set).

name: set_track_subject
title: Lock the camera on someone
description: Aim-lock the shot camera onto an entity: the camera stays pointed at it no matter how its position moves (marks, recordings, presets). Pass no entityId to turn tracking off.

entityId.description: Entity id to track; omit to disable tracking.

name: snap_to_ground
title: Put something on the ground
description: Drop an entity so it rests on the ground plane (y = 0 at its feet).

name: set_time
title: Jump to a time
description: Scrub the timeline playhead to time t (seconds).

name: play
title: Play
description: Start timeline playback from the current playhead.

name: stop
title: Stop
description: Stop timeline playback.

name: screenshot
title: Look at the shot
description: Capture the current viewport as a PNG image and return it. Use after staging or scrubbing to see what the shot looks like.

name: list_presets
title: List saved stages
description: List saved global stage presets (reusable staging setups) as { id, name, savedAt, entityCount }.

name: save_preset
title: Save this stage
description: Save the current staging as a named global preset for reuse across projects.

name: apply_preset
title: Load a saved stage
description: Load a saved stage preset by id into the current scene.

name: import_scan
title: Import a 3D scan
description: Import a Gaussian-splat / photogrammetry scan (.ply/.splat/.spz/.ksplat) as an environment. The file is copied into the project's scans/ folder and attached to the current scene. Scans are editor-only reference geometry — visible while you block, never rendered into any export pass. Returns the created scan (id, name, transform).

sourcePath.description: Absolute path to the scan file (.ply/.splat/.spz/.ksplat).

name: set_scan_transform
title: Move or scale a scan
description: Position, rotate, scale, flip, or show/hide an imported scan. Omitted fields are left unchanged; position merges onto the current position. Set flipped:true to right an upside-down .splat export.

scanId.description: Scan id from get_state or import_scan.

position.description: World position (partial; merged onto the current position).

rotationDeg.description: Yaw in degrees, counter-clockwise seen from above.

flipped.description: Pitch the scan 180° to right upside-down (Y-down) .splat exports.

name: remove_scan
title: Remove a scan
description: Remove an imported scan from the current scene (the copied file is left on disk).

scanId.description: Scan id from get_state or import_scan.

name: set_reference
title: Attach a reference video
description: Attach a reference video to the active shot (the Motion Previs Studio handoff v1). The clip is copied into the project’s refs/ folder and shown as a ghost underlay (or picture-in-picture) so you can match blocking against it by eye. videoPath is an absolute path to the source clip.

handoffVersion.description: Motion Previs handoff protocol version. Omit only for legacy clients.

videoPath.description: Absolute path to the reference video file.

mode.description: Underlay style: ghost overlay (default) or picture-in-picture.

name: new_scene
title: Add a scene
description: Add a new scene (a new location or setup) after the last one and switch to it. It starts with one empty shot. Returns the new scene and shot ids.

name: select_scene
title: Switch scene
description: Switch to another scene and its first shot. Scene ids are in get_state (allScenes).

name: select_shot
title: Switch shot
description: Switch to another shot (switching scene too if the shot is in another scene). Shot ids are in get_state (allScenes).

name: set_lighting
title: Change the lighting
description: Change the current scene's lighting. Presets: day, goldenHour, night, interiorWarm, interiorCool, club, and the physical-sky presets middaySky, goldenHourSky, blueHourSky. Sun angles are in degrees. Returns the new environment.

sunElevationDeg.description: Optional sun height above the horizon in degrees (about 6-86).

name: set_entity_style
title: Change how something looks
description: Change an entity's label, colour, name, height or build (people only), or hide it from exports (it stays visible in the editor). Give each character a different colour and a short label so the video model can tell them apart. Colours: red, amber, green, blue, purple, pink, teal, orange, or a hex value. Omitted fields are unchanged; an empty label removes it. Returns the entity, with notes when a value was clamped or ignored.

label.description: Short uppercase label, e.g. "HERO". Empty removes the label.

color.description: red, amber, green, blue, purple, pink, teal, orange, or a hex value like "#e5484d".

heightScale.description: People only: height scale 0.8..1.2 (1 = default); values outside are clamped. Other assets ignore it.

build.description: People only: build 0.8..1.3 (1 = default); values outside are clamped. Other assets ignore it.

hideInExports.description: true hides it in every export pass.

name: set_camera_rig
title: Change the camera rig
description: Set what the shot camera is mounted on: sticks (tripod), dolly, steadicam, handheld, crane, drone or carMount. intensity 0..1 scales the shake or drift.

name: list_marks
title: List timeline marks
description: List the marks on one timeline lane — the shot camera ("camera") or one entity — sorted by time, with the ids update_mark and delete_marks take. Angles in degrees.

lane.description: "camera" for the shot camera, or an entity id from get_state for that performer.

name: update_mark
title: Edit a timeline mark
description: Change one mark. Omitted fields are unchanged; time is kept inside the shot. Camera marks take panDeg/tiltDeg/rollDeg/focalLength/focusDistance; actor marks take gait. Mark ids come from list_marks. A camera mark framed by shot words (it has a shot, from frame_shot) is re-solved every frame, so its pose (x/y/z/panDeg/tiltDeg/rollDeg, and focalLength when the words set the lens or an over-the-shoulder) needs release: true first; time, hold and eases don't.

lane.description: "camera" for the shot camera, or an entity id from get_state for that performer.

gait.description: Actor marks: movement style approaching this mark.

hold.description: Seconds to stay on the mark after arriving.

panDeg.description: Camera: pan in degrees, counter-clockwise seen from above; 0 faces -Z, 90 faces -X.

tiltDeg.description: Camera: tilt in degrees; positive up.

release.description: Camera marks framed by shot words: true freezes the current framing into a plain mark (drops the words), then applies the other fields. Undo brings the words back.

name: delete_marks
title: Delete timeline marks
description: Delete marks from one lane by id (ids from list_marks). Undo brings them back.

lane.description: "camera" for the shot camera, or an entity id from get_state for that performer.

name: apply_motion
title: Give performers a move
description: Give people a single-performer motion from the motion library (a punch, a dance step, a gesture…), replacing their marks. Motion ids come from list_motion_presets; only person entities move.

name: undo
title: Undo
description: Undo the last change to the project.

name: redo
title: Redo
description: Redo the last undone change.

name: save_project
title: Save the project
description: Save the project to its folder now (the app also autosaves).

name: list_export_profiles
title: List export targets
description: List the AI video and image models Blockout can export for, with their maximum and recommended shot length, aspect ratios, frame rate, input-file and prompt caps, and what to attach where. Use an id with export_shot.

name: export_shot
title: Export the shot
description: Export the active shot as a clean blockout package for an AI video model: the reference video, a depth video, stills at every camera mark, and a prompt tailored to the target that says what each grey shape is, what happens and what the camera does. Takes a while for long shots. Call screenshot first to check the framing. Returns the package folder, its path inside the project, the prompt, and warnings for any limit of the target the shot breaks (too long, an aspect it does not take).

profileId.description: Export target id from list_export_profiles (default "seedance-2"; "minimax-h3-max" for MiniMax H3 Max 3D to Video).

labels.description: Name labels over people: on (videos and stills), stillsOnly (default), or off.

resolution.description: Output size: auto (the target's native size, default), or pin the short edge to 720p / 1080p.

name: export_frame
title: Export this frame
description: Export the frame at the playhead as a full-quality PNG (a key pose or the moment of impact). Returns the file path.

profileId.description: Export target id from list_export_profiles (default "seedance-2"; "minimax-h3-max" for MiniMax H3 Max 3D to Video).

resolution.description: Output size: auto (the target's native size, default), or pin the short edge to 720p / 1080p.

labels.description: Show name labels (default false, like the exported clip).

name: export_contact_sheet
title: Export a contact sheet
description: Export one PNG with the first frame of every shot in the current scene, captioned with lens, length and aspect. Returns the file path (contact-sheet-<date-time>.png in the scene's exports folder, so an earlier sheet is never overwritten).

name: export_scene_animatic
title: Export the scene animatic
description: Export every shot in the current scene in order and join them into one animatic video. Every shot must share the same aspect ratio and frame rate. Returns the video's path (animatic-<date-time>.mp4, so an earlier animatic is never overwritten).

profileId.description: Export target id from list_export_profiles (default "seedance-2"; "minimax-h3-max" for MiniMax H3 Max 3D to Video).

resolution.description: Output size: auto (the target's native size, default), or pin the short edge to 720p / 1080p.
